messages.content: What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?

message.content: Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) belong to very different lineages—lions are felids (order Carnivora) while zebras are equids (order Perissodactyla). Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the two orders, which lies within the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**. This ancestor would have been a small, generalized placental mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago, during the late Cretaceous to early Paleogene. In other words, the common ancestor of lion and zebra is a basal Laurasiatherian mammal, not a more specific ancestor such as a particular genus or family.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want the common ancestor of lion and zebra. We need to answer. The question is about evolutionary biology. Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga). They belong to different families: lions are Felidae (cat family), zebras are Equidae (horse family). Both are mammals, order Carnivora vs order Perissodactyla? Actually zebra is an odd-toed ungulate, order Perissodactyla. Lions are carnivores, order Carnivora. So their common ancestor would be at the level of mammals, perhaps the last common ancestor of placental mammals. But maybe they want the common ancestor at the level of the last common ancestor of the two species, which is the last common ancestor of the Felidae and Equidae. That would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That is the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatheria? Actually Carnivora and Perissodactyla are both part of Laurasiatheria. So the last common ancestor of those two orders would be the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria. That might be the last common ancestor of the group that includes Carnivora, Perissodactyla, Cetartiodactyla, Chiroptera, Eulipotyphla, etc. So the common ancestor would be a mammal from the late Cretaceous or early Paleogene. But maybe the answer: "They share a common ancestor at the level of placental mammals, specifically the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatheria clade." Or "the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which lived around 70 million years ago." So we can answer accordingly.
